summary.tldr: Requires online platforms to prevent and remove fraudulent content, notify users who saw it, and adds a sentencing factor for identity theft or fraud against vulnerable victims.
what_it_does: Requires owners and operators of online services and apps to take reasonable steps in how they are designed and run to prevent fraudulent content from being spread.
Requires operators to remove content that has been identified as fraudulent and to notify users they know or should reasonably know engaged with it.
Requires operators to keep records of removed content and notices sent, and to publish reports with prescribed information.
Makes breaking these rules an offence punishable on summary conviction by a fine of up to $1 million, unless the operator can show due diligence.
Adds a Criminal Code sentencing factor for identity theft or identity fraud committed against a victim made vulnerable by their age, health or financial situation.
who_it_affects: Victims of identity theft or fraud
summary.background: The bill defines “operator” to include owners or operators of online services or applications that connect to the Internet. It also amends the Criminal Code to add a sentencing factor for identity theft or identity fraud against vulnerable victims.
